title: xswap swap-in readahead: rounds 1–3
subtitle: protocol rev7 (not approved) · tool code unmerged · guest 4 vCPU / 4096 MiB / swap 16 GiB · QEMU TCG · draft 2026-10-29

verdict.headline: No candidate accepted: c1 worsened zram tails, clock faults cut c1c short, and round 3 (c1d) did not run. Continuing needs a protocol fix; Hurric decides.

sections.title: Why
sections.lead: Touching a swapped-out page stalls until the kernel reads it back.

blocks.takeaway: Every swap-in makes the program wait

blocks.text: Hypothesis: read neighbouring pages too (readahead) so later faults hit.

blocks.takeaway: Under memory pressure cold pages go to two backends
blocks.label: guest kernel

blocks.takeaway: Only the readahead decision changes
blocks.label: fault handler

blocks.takeaway: Step through: c1 reads ahead on both, c1c on disk only
blocks.label: sequential A→B→C
blocks.tradeoff: Inference: readahead saves later waits but costs the first fault; zram is sync, so the cost lands in the tail.
blocks.static: c1 reads ahead on disk and zram; c1c on disk only.
